title: Evaluation Pitfalls and Metric Masking
summary: Work through Evaluation Pitfalls and Metric Masking.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **Evaluation Pitfalls and Metric Masking** in *Closed-Loop Evaluation* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, Closed-Loop Evaluation, § Evaluation Pitfalls and Metric Masking
blocks.md: A physical qualification report can present a spotless pass rate and an exact confidence bound while still misrepresenting what the machine can safely do, if the test procedure quietly narrowed the operating domain, tuned weights on the test unit, or discarded inconvenient runs before the bound was computed. Systematic errors undermining policy evaluation rarely stem from deliberate fraud; they arise when an evaluation protocol answers an easier question than the claim asks, creating statistical or procedural mirages that mask physical vulnerability.

questions.q: The section **Evaluation Pitfalls and Metric Masking** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Hazards are rates per operating hour, and bounding a rate lambda with zero events needs about 3/lambda failure-free hours, so rare hazards cannot be demonstrated by sampling the proposer.

Shadow operation runs the candidate on the real machine while the baseline keeps authority, so the candidate's inputs stay confined to the baseline's state distribution and its recovery is never tested.

The evaluation record binds a bounded claim to its target ODD, configuration digests, sampling protocol, complete outcome log, exact statistics, and the catalog of unsupported gaps, which become runtime obligations.
Task completion, proposer autonomy, and supervisory burden are separate channels, and an intervened run is an autonomy failure, never a success that was cut short (the censored trial fallacy).
